Pap smears with glandular cell abnormalities are often flagged as abnormal by Rapid Papanicolaou (RPS) screening. This means that even if these results are not significantly abnormal, they can still be considered abnormal by the RPS, resulting in a sensitivity of 36.4% at the AGC threshold. However, some cases of glandular cell abnormalities may only be detected on Pap smears by RPS, indicating that this method is valuable for identifying abnormal cells.

To improve adherence to follow-up recommendations and reduce missed cancers, using up to 3 reminders can be effective. Allocating resources to more effective methods for improving patient adherence to follow-up care may be more important than recommending specific procedures for managing abnormal Pap smear results.
